name: CloudinaryFiles
title: Cloudinary Files
description: List media already stored in Cloudinary, optionally filtered by folder or tag.
whenToUse: Find assets ALREADY in Cloudinary — browse a folder, pull everything with a tag, or take a random selection for a gallery. It reads an existing library rather than creating anything, so pair it with Cloudinary Upload when the asset does not exist yet.

inputs.name: signal
inputs.description: Trigger. The filters come from config.

outputs.name: files
outputs.description: Matching assets, each with public_id, urls, dimensions, tags and a universalId

folder.title: Folder
folder.description: Only assets whose public id starts with this. Leave blank for the whole account.

maxFiles.title: Max Files
maxFiles.description: How many to return, up to Cloudinary's 500 per request

tags.title: Tag
tags.description: Only assets carrying this tag. Leave blank for all.

randomSelection.title: Random Selection
randomSelection.description: Shuffle before trimming to Max Files, so repeated runs surface different assets. Only has an effect when more were found than Max Files.

authRequired.title: Require sign-in
authRequired.description: Only a signed-in caller may run this step. Leave off and it runs for whoever the workflow's trigger admitted, which is the usual answer.

authRole.title: Require role
authRole.description: A claim the caller's account must carry, as noun:verb (finance:approve, payments:refund). Leave blank to require only that they are signed in.

package.name: cloudinary
package.packageFile:
$schema: ../_schema/package.schema.json

# CLOUDINARY, fully declarative.
#
# It sat on the backlog as "blocked on `encoding: form`", and that turned out to be wrong twice over. The
# nodes used the Cloudinary SDK, so the blocker was inferred from the SDK's behaviour rather than from the
# HTTP API — and the HTTP API is kinder than the SDK:
#
#   SIGNING IS OPTIONAL. The SDK signs every upload (sorted params + api_secret, SHA-1), which the
#   expression sandbox cannot do — it has sha256 and no sha1. Cloudinary's docs offer HTTP Basic Auth
#   instead, explicitly "no signature calculation required", for the Upload API as well as the Admin API.
#   So `scheme: basic`, which already existed.
#
#   THE UPLOAD BODY IS A FORM, and their own curl example uses -F, which is multipart — the capability
#   built for ElevenLabs speech-to-text a moment earlier. `encoding: form` was never needed.
#
# The lesson is the one already recorded in the backlog: judge by the WIRE FORMAT, never by the client
# library a node happened to use.

name: cloudinary
displayName: Cloudinary
description: Upload, list and read media in Cloudinary
version: 2.0.0
category: media
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1754502687/gravity/icons/cloudinary_logo.png

features:
  - Upload images and video from a URL or base64
  - List and read media already in the account

allowedHosts:
  - api.cloudinary.com

requires:
  executorVersion: ">=1.6.0"
  credential: [basic]
  transport: [json]
  encoding: [multipart]

credentials.cloudinaryCredential.yaml:
$schema: ../../_schema/credential.schema.json

# FIELD NAMES ARE SNAKE_CASE, unchanged, because that is what the stored credentials use — a credential is
# read by field name, so tidying these to camelCase would leave every existing workflow authenticating
# with three undefineds.
name: cloudinaryCredential
displayName: Cloudinary
description: Cloudinary API credentials for media management

properties:
  - name: cloud_name
    displayName: Cloud Name
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: false
    description: Your Cloudinary cloud name
  - name: api_key
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    # Was false, so this was stored in PLAINTEXT (SECURITY.md, 2026-08-30). Cloudinary signs
    # requests with api_key + api_secret together, so the pair IS the credential; treating
    # half of it as public is a distinction the database cannot act on. Only cloud_name is
    # genuinely public here, because it appears in every delivery URL.
    secret: true
    description: Your Cloudinary API key
  - name: api_secret
    displayName: API Secret
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Cloudinary API secret

shared.credential.yaml:
# BASIC AUTH, and it is the reason this package needed no new capability.
#
# The SDK these nodes used signs every upload: sorted params, appended api_secret, SHA-1 — and the sandbox
# has no sha1, so that path would have needed a signing scheme in the executor. Cloudinary's own docs
# offer a way out: "Authenticate using your API Key and API Secret via HTTP Basic Auth (no signature
# calculation required)". Both the Admin API and the Upload API accept it.
#
# So all three nodes authenticate the same way, and the executor already had `basic`.

scheme: basic
username: "{{ credentials.cloudinaryCredential.api_key }}"
password: "{{ credentials.cloudinaryCredential.api_secret }}"

files.api/run.yaml:
# ONE GET to the ADMIN API, with Basic Auth — which the Admin API has always accepted, so this node was
# never really blocked on anything.
#
# `prefix` IS THE FOLDER FILTER. Cloudinary has no folder parameter on this endpoint: a folder is just a
# public-id prefix, which is why the service set `prefix` from `config.folder`. Transcribed rather than
# renamed, because `folder` would be silently ignored.

- name: resources
  method: GET
  url: >-
    return 'https://api.cloudinary.com/v1_1/'
      + credentials.cloudinaryCredential.cloud_name
      + '/resources/' + (config.resourceType || 'image')
  credential: { $ref: credential }

  query:
    # `type: upload` excludes fetched and private assets, matching the service.
    type: upload
    max_results: "return config.maxFiles || 100"
    prefix: "{{ config.folder }}"
    tags: "{{ config.tags }}"

  transport: json

  error:
    when: "return !!response.error"
    message: "return response.error.message || 'Cloudinary listing failed'"
files.config.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/config.schema.json

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: []
  properties:
    folder:
      type: string
      title: Folder
      description: Only assets whose public id starts with this. Leave blank for the whole account.
      default: ""
    maxFiles:
      type: number
      title: Max Files
      description: How many to return, up to Cloudinary's 500 per request
      default: 100
      minimum: 1
      maximum: 500
    resourceType:
      type: string
      title: Resource Type
      enum: [image, video, raw]
      enumNames: [Image, Video, Raw]
      default: image
    tags:
      type: string
      title: Tag
      description: Only assets carrying this tag. Leave blank for all.
      default: ""
    randomSelection:
      type: boolean
      title: Random Selection
      description: >-
        Shuffle before trimming to Max Files, so repeated runs surface different assets. Only has an effect
        when more were found than Max Files.
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle
"ui:order": [folder, tags, resourceType, maxFiles, randomSelection]
files.interface.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/interface.schema.json

inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: object
    description: Trigger. The filters come from config.
    required: false

outputs:
  - name: files
    type: array
    description: Matching assets, each with public_id, urls, dimensions, tags and a universalId
  - name: count
    type: number
    description: How many assets were returned

credentials:
  - name: cloudinaryCredential
    required: true
files.node.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/node.schema.json

type: CloudinaryFiles
kind: PromiseNode

name: Cloudinary Files
category: Media & Design
color: "#3448C5"
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1754502687/gravity/icons/cloudinary_logo.png

description: List media already stored in Cloudinary, optionally filtered by folder or tag.

whenToUse: >-
  Find assets ALREADY in Cloudinary — browse a folder, pull everything with a tag, or take a random
  selection for a gallery. It reads an existing library rather than creating anything, so pair it with
  Cloudinary Upload when the asset does not exist yet.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # NOT cacheable: a library changes as things are uploaded, and random selection is meant to differ.
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/test.schema.json

# Needs CLOUDINARY_CLOUD_NAME, CLOUDINARY_API_KEY and CLOUDINARY_API_SECRET. Read-only — it lists and
# writes nothing.

testData:
  config:
    maxFiles: 5
    resourceType: image
    randomSelection: false
  inputs:
    signal: {}
  expect:
    # An ARRAY, and the cap honoured. A listing that ignored max_results would still look like a success.
    files: "return Array.isArray(output.files) && output.files.length <= 5"
    count: "return output.count === output.files.length"
